entries.note: Neither an AI SaaS 'story' nor everything riding on GPU sales has a shared, sufficiently definite test.
'Not enough money in the world' is hyperbole about funding requirements, without a specified funding horizon or amount.

entries.test: Public GPU inventory and installation records would establish whether millions awaited installation, while financing and investment-return records would test the asserted debt dependence and purchasing economics.
entries.note: This bundles a concrete inventory claim with debt dependence and an investment judgment. Observation best captures its factual core; the final clause is evaluative.

entries.test: OpenAI's cumulative revenue through September 2025 and contemporaneous reporting of its first-half revenue would settle the numerical assertions.
entries.note: The surrounding retrospective supports the supplied year, 2025.

entries.test: Public records comparing cumulative AI revenue attributable to the NVIDIA GPU purchases under discussion with their acquisition costs would show whether those costs were ever recovered.
entries.note: Payback would falsify 'never'; retirement without payback could settle the claim for the relevant GPUs.

entries.test: The contract's payment and service requirements, together with OpenAI's financial resources and Oracle's available capacity as of September 12, 2025, would test both assertions.
entries.note: The proposition preserves the historical assessment rather than asserting that subsequent financing or capacity expansion was impossible.

entries.test: Public contract obligations and implementation costs would establish whether carrying out the agreed compute and data center plans required at least $1 trillion during the four years following September 26, 2025.
entries.note: The forward funding requirement is conditional on executing the plans. Its four-year horizon ends September 26, 2029.
The normalization weakens his stated expectation into 'likely.' The original lacks a shared test for the population, exaggerated enthusiasm, or eventual acceptance.
